Saudi Water Bill Calculator (New 2027 Tariff)

Enter your monthly consumption in cubic metres and your meter size to see the bill under the new tariff, each tier, and the difference from the current tariff.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

Calculate your bill

From your bill or the NWC app. A typical household uses about 20 to 30 m³.
SAR 20 for water and 10 for sewage are added for each unit after the first.

New residential water tariff from 1 January 2027

Monthly consumptionWater (SAR/m³)Sewage (SAR/m³)TotalCurrent (total)

The tiers are progressive: each cubic metre is charged at its own tier's rate, not at the highest rate. The current tariff has five tiers; the new one has four.

New fixed monthly fees by meter size

Meter sizeResidential: water + sewageNon-residential: water + sewage
Up to 20 mm20 + 10 = SAR 3040 + 20 = SAR 60
21–40 mm40 + 20 = SAR 6060 + 30 = SAR 90
41–65 mm60 + 30 = SAR 9080 + 40 = SAR 120
66–100 mm80 + 40 = SAR 120100 + 50 = SAR 150
Over 100 mm100 + 50 = SAR 150150 + 75 = SAR 225

Homes pay SAR 20 for water and 10 for sewage for each additional unit. Government accounts pay fixed fees of SAR 1,000 for water and 500 for sewage, and SAR 10 per m³ for water and 5 for sewage.

Example: a home with a 20 mm meter uses 30 m³ in a month.

Water: 15 × 1 + 15 × 2 = SAR 45. Sewage: half of that, SAR 22.50. Fixed fees: 20 + 10 = SAR 30.
SAR 97.50 before tax, and SAR 112.13 with 15% VAT.
Under the current tariff: 15 × 0.10 + 15 × 1 = SAR 16.50 for water and 8.25 for sewage, SAR 24.75 in all, or SAR 28.46 with VAT (without any current meter fee).

Before you rely on the figure

  • The new figures come from the National Water Company's announcement as reported by the press; your official bill is the reference.
  • The comparison with the current tariff leaves out any meter fee on your current bill, because its amount is not published.
  • Bills that span 2026 and 2027 charge consumption before 1 January 2027 at the current tariff and the rest at the new one.

For electricity, use the Saudi electricity bill calculator. Prefer Arabic? Use the Arabic version.

Frequently asked questions

What is the new water tariff for homes in Saudi Arabia?

From 1 January 2027, residential: SAR 1 per cubic metre from 0 to 15 m³ a month, SAR 2 for the part above 15 up to 30, SAR 4 above 30 up to 45, and SAR 6 above 45. Sewage is added at half those rates, so the totals are SAR 1.5, 3, 6 and 9 per m³.

Is all my consumption charged at the highest tier?

No. Each cubic metre is charged at the rate of the tier it falls in. At 30 m³ you pay 15 m³ at SAR 1 and 15 m³ at SAR 2 for water, SAR 45 in all, plus SAR 22.50 for sewage.

What are the new fixed meter fees?

A monthly fee for the main residential unit by meter diameter: up to 20 mm SAR 20 for water and 10 for sewage; 21–40 mm 40 and 20; 41–65 mm 60 and 30; 66–100 mm 80 and 40; over 100 mm 100 and 50. Each additional unit adds SAR 20 for water and 10 for sewage.

What was the old water tariff?

Since 2016: 10 halalas per m³ up to 15 m³, SAR 1 up to 30, SAR 3 up to 45, SAR 4 up to 60 and SAR 6 above, with sewage at 50% of the water charge where the service is available.

Is VAT added?

VAT of 15% is added to water bills. The announced figures do not mention VAT, so the calculator adds it to both consumption and fixed fees; you can switch it off to see the amount before tax.

What if my home is not connected to the sewage network?

Under the current tariff sewage is charged only where the service is available. The new tariff announcement does not say this explicitly, so choose “No” to see the bill without sewage charges.

What are the non-residential and government rates?

Non-residential: one tier of SAR 8 per m³ for water and 4 for sewage, with a fixed fee of SAR 40 to 150 for water by meter size and half that for sewage. Government: SAR 10 for water and 5 for sewage, with fixed fees of SAR 1,000 and 500. Industrial and agricultural use is not covered by the change.

What is the SAR 500 monthly support?

Alongside the electricity and water tariff changes, a royal directive grants SAR 500 a month to civil and military state employees, retirees, family members of deceased insured people and retirees, and social security families. GOSI said retirees will receive it automatically from 1 January 2027.
